column20: intro paragraph: the incident was a result of a surge of traffic from a single customer that overloaded Cloudflare's links with AWS us-east-1
column21: Background: some edge router links to an AWS peering switch had insufficient capacity; queues on the routers grew significantly and began dropping packets
column22: intro paragraph: This was a regional problem between Cloudflare and AWS us-east-1; customers with origins in AWS us-east-1 experienced impact
column23: intro paragraph: This was a regional problem between Cloudflare and AWS us-east-1, and global Cloudflare services were not affected
column24: What happened: AWS withdrawals rerouted traffic to an additional set of peering links connected via an offsite switch which subsequently also became saturated; one direct peering link was at half-capacity from a pre-existing failure
column25: after Timeline: This was handled by manual traffic actions both from Cloudflare and AWS; rate limiting of the single customer at 19:05 and traffic engineering at 19:27
column26: intro paragraph: global Cloudflare services were not affected; impact attributed to link congestion and manual BGP traffic engineering, no centralised controller named
column27: V8a: Remediations and follow-up steps - necessity of architecting for better customer isolation to prevent any single entity from monopolizing shared resources; V8b and V8c: no statement found
column28: V9 uses timeline IMPACT START 16:27 to IMPACT END 20:18; report also notes substantial reduction by 19:38.
